## Key terms

{{< glossary rotation rotation-matrix angle radian pivot transformation inverse-matrix angular-speed matrix-multiplication unit-circle >}}

## 12.1 Turn a point around the origin

- A **rotation** by θ around the origin:
  **x' = x cos θ − y sin θ**, **y' = x sin θ + y cos θ**.
- A positive θ turns anticlockwise. The distance from the origin stays the
  same.
- Blade tip (4, 0), 30° (cos 0.87, sin 0.5): (3.46, 2).
- (3, 1) by 90° (cos 0, sin 1): (−1, 3), the spell Turn of lecture 10.

![Rotating a point around the origin.](images/rotate-point.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/rotate-lab.html" poster="sims/rotate-lab.png" title="Rotate Lab: R(θ) and the pivot" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The minus sign is in x'. Without it the point turns clockwise.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Rotate by hand, check in the lab"}
On paper, rotate (2, 2) by 90° and by 180° around the origin. Then check both
in **Rotate Lab** with the pivot at the origin.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Rotate a point"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 4.35)|(1, −3)"}
Rotate (5, 0) by 30° (cos 0.87, sin 0.5).
:   (4.35, 2.5)

Rotate (3, 1) by 180°.
:   (−3, −1)

Rotate (0, 2) by 90°.
:   (−2, 0)

Rotate (3, 1) by 90°.
:   (−1, 3)

What stays the same in a rotation around the origin?
:   the distance from the origin
:::
:::

## 12.2 The rotation matrix

- **R(θ) = rows (cos θ, −sin θ) and (sin θ, cos θ)**.
- R(θ) × (x, y) gives the formulas of 12.1.
- Its columns: (1, 0) goes to (cos θ, sin θ); (0, 1) goes to
  (−sin θ, cos θ).
- R(90°) = rows (0, −1), (1, 0). R(180°) = rows (−1, 0), (0, −1).
  R(30°) = rows (0.87, −0.5), (0.5, 0.87).
- R(30°) × (2, 2) = (1.74 − 1, 1 + 1.74) = (0.74, 2.74).

![The columns of R(θ).](images/rotation-matrix.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
−sin θ is in row 1, column 2. Check: R(90°) must send (1, 0) to (0, 1).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build R(45°)"}
cos 45° = sin 45° = 0.71. Write R(45°) and multiply it by (2, 0). Is the
length still 2?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The matrix"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="rows (0, 1) and (1, 0)|rows (1, 0) and (0, 1)"}
Which matrix is R(90°)?
:   rows (0, −1) and (1, 0)

Which matrix is R(180°)?
:   rows (−1, 0) and (0, −1)

Where does R(θ) send (1, 0)?
:   (cos θ, sin θ)

What is R(90°) × (2, −1)?
:   (1, 2)

Where is −sin θ in R(θ)?
:   row 1, column 2
:::
:::

## 12.3 Turn the drawbridge: rotation about a pivot

- About the pivot C: **P' = C + R(θ) (P − C)**: move by −C, rotate, move
  back.
- The drawbridge: hinge H = (2, 1), end E = (6, 1). E − H = (4, 0).
- 90°: (0, 4) + H = **(2, 5)**. 30°: (3.46, 2) + H = **(5.46, 3)**.
- Rotating E itself around the origin gives (−1, 6): the bridge flies away.

![The drawbridge turns about its hinge.](images/rotate-pivot.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Subtract the pivot first, and add it back at the end.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A pivot in Rotate Lab"}
Tap the grid at (1, 0) to move the pivot. Set θ = 90° and read P' for
P = (2, 2). Check by hand: P − C, R(90°), + C.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · About a pivot"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(−2, 5)|(5, 0)"}
Rotate (5, 2) by 90° about (3, 2).
:   (3, 4)

A door: hinge (1, 1), handle (1, 3). Turn by −90° about the hinge.
:   (3, 1)

The drawbridge (H = (2, 1), E = (6, 1)) turns 90°. Where is the end?
:   (2, 5)

What is step 1 of a rotation about a pivot C?
:   subtract C
:::
:::

## 12.4 What a rotation keeps, and how to undo it

- A rotation keeps every **length** and every **angle**. Only directions
  change.
- **Undo: R(θ)^−1^ = R(−θ)**: turn back by the same angle.
- R(−θ) is the transpose of R(θ): rows become columns.
  R(−30°) = rows (0.87, 0.5), (−0.5, 0.87).
- det R(θ) = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1: no squashing, always an inverse.

![A rotation keeps lengths and angles.](images/rotate-keeps.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
To undo 30°, turn −30°, not another 30°.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Lengths stay"}
Rotate the triangle (1, 1), (4, 1), (1, 3) by 90°. Compute the length of the
side from (1, 1) to (4, 1) before and after.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Keep and undo"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="R(30°)|2"}
Which matrix undoes R(30°)?
:   R(−30°)

What is the determinant of a rotation matrix?
:   1

What does a rotation change?
:   the direction

Which matrix is R(−90°)?
:   rows (0, 1) and (−1, 0)

A gun of length 2 turns by 45°. How long is it now?
:   still 2
:::
:::

## 12.5 A little turn every frame

- Turn per frame: **Δθ = ω × Δt** (angular speed × frame time, lecture 8).
- Windmill 180°/s at 60 fps: 3° per frame; after 30 frames, 90°. At 30 fps:
  6° per frame, the same speed.
- Unity: `transform.Rotate(0, 0, 180 * Time.deltaTime);`
- `Quaternion.Euler(0, 0, 30) * new Vector3(4, 0, 0)` gives (3.46, 2, 0). A
  positive angle around z turns anticlockwise in 2D.

![A little rotation every frame.](images/spin-frame.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"3° every frame" without Δt makes the windmill turn twice as fast at 120 fps.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The turret"}
A turret turns at 90°/s, at 30 fps. How many degrees per frame, and how many
frames for a quarter turn? Where is the gun tip (2, 0) after the quarter
turn?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Every frame"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="60°|2°"}
A wheel turns at 360°/s. How many degrees per frame at 60 fps?
:   6°

A windmill turns at 180°/s. How many degrees per frame at 30 fps?
:   6°

Why multiply by Time.deltaTime?
:   the speed does not depend on the frame rate

A turret at 90°/s, 30 fps. How many frames for a quarter turn?
:   30
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Drawbridge {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Drawbridge** is a castle game. The bridge turns around its hinge
**H = (2, 1)**; it is 4 units long; lying flat, its end is at **E = (6, 1)**.
A ship needs the end at (2, 5); a knight needs it on the ledge at
(5.46, 3).

{{< sim file="sims/drawbridge.html" poster="sims/drawbridge.png" title="Drawbridge: turn the bridge about its hinge" kind="game" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · The bridge"}
H = (2, 1), E = (6, 1), so E − H = (4, 0). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="45°|−90°"}
Which turn puts the end at (2, 5)?
:   90°

Which turn puts the end at (5.46, 3)?
:   30°

Where is the end at 180°?
:   (−2, 1)

Where is the end at −90°?
:   (2, −3)
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · Back down (harder)"}
H = (2, 1), the bridge is 4 long. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="60°|(6, 5)"}
The bridge stands at 60°. Which turn brings it back flat?
:   −60°

The bridge goes up at 45°/s at 60 fps. How many degrees per frame?
:   0.75°

At 60°, where is the end? (cos 60° = 0.5, sin 60° = 0.87)
:   (4, 4.48)

A player turns the bridge by 90° around the origin by mistake. Where does the end (6, 1) go?
:   (−1, 6)
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- A rotation by θ: x' = x cos θ − y sin θ, y' = x sin θ + y cos θ.
- R(θ) = rows (cos θ, −sin θ), (sin θ, cos θ); its columns are the turned axes.
- About a pivot: P' = C + R(θ)(P − C).
- A rotation keeps lengths and angles; R(−θ) undoes it.
- In the game loop, turn by ω × Δt each frame.
